Subject: Production throughput degradation on dedicated pool (BrightHealth AI)

Hi Laura,

We started seeing a ~30% sustained throughput drop across our Inference endpoints backed by the dedicated Redwood pool (~08:30 PST). Error rates are low, but tail latency and overall p50/p95 tokens/sec have dropped and a lot of requests are getting queued. This started gradually then worsened over ~20 minutes.

Affected models: redwood-3b-quant-v2 on shard group bhai-3b-prd. Endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/chat/generate. We attached a short sample of request timestamps and response timings.

We're in a production window and this is impacting real traffic. Can you confirm whether this is an autoscaling issue or GPU-worker saturation? Please advise immediate mitigation steps and an approximate ETA for a resolution.

Thanks,
Samantha Bright
Head of Platform Engineering
BrightHealth AI

- sample-reqs.log (text)

Hi Samantha —

Thanks for the heads-up and for the log sample. We're on this. Quick summary of next actions we propose (need your sign-off to proceed with traffic reroute):

1) Immediate: enable cross-region fallback to our hosted pool for a subset of traffic (canary 10%) to lift immediate pressure while keeping your primary route intact.
2) Short term (30–60m): execute a rolling worker restart across the dedicated shard group to clear KV-cache pressure and rebalance batch queues. No model version changes.
3) Post-recovery: run a focused postmortem and share remediation steps (autoscaler tuning + prefix-cache warmup).

If you approve step (1) we'll proceed immediately and keep you posted every 15 minutes.

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:31:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: rolling recovery plan (BrightHealth AI) — immediate execution checklist

Team —

Summary: BrightHealth is seeing degraded throughput on their dedicated pool. External contact (Samantha) consented to a canary fallback. I'm proposing we run the following rolling recovery that minimizes impact and avoids a full failover. Please review and ack.

Proposed rolling recovery (ordered steps):
- Step A (t+0m): 10% traffic reroute to hosted pool (route-by-slo policy). Monitor p50/p95 and error spike.
- Step B (t+10m): drain 1 worker from shard bhai-3b-prd and restart it (clear KV cache + restart runtime). Wait 3m health checks. Repeat 1 worker every 6 minutes across the pool to avoid cache stampede.
- Step C (t+40m): if metrics improving (p95 tokens/sec + <5% queuing), increase reroute back to 0% and keep warm standby nodes spun for 60m.
- Step D (post recovery): collect traces, upload collection to the incident page, and schedule autoscaler tuning (increase min-replicas and change reaction-time window).

Attachments: recovery-runbook-v1.pdf (internal runbook + checklists).

Customer comms: I'll send status every 15 minutes and a final postmortem within 48 hours.

Priority: high. Marcus, can you lead the worker restarts and verify health checks? Monica, can you prepare the postmortem skeleton and cost/credit implications?

Laura

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Internal: rolling recovery plan (BrightHealth AI) — immediate execution checklist

Ack. Quick technical notes from my side after an initial probe:
- Root cause signal: sudden KV cache pressure (large prefix-miss storm triggered by a batch of batched inference requests with atypical prompt lengths). This caused sustained memory pressure that forced our per-worker request queue to grow and reduced throughput.
- Autoscaler behavior: the autoscaler target was based on average GPU util and missed the rapid queue growth — by the time util rose the queue was already long. We should adjust scaling to consider request-queue length and kv-miss-rate as second-order signals.

Immediate ops plan (will execute):
1) Start the 10% cross-region reroute now.
2) Rolling restart of workers as you described; I'll stagger restarts and monitor queue depth.
3) If any worker fails health checks twice, we will remove it from the shard and increase canary to 25% temporarily.

ETA: first measurable improvement expected 12–18 minutes after canary reroute.

I'll push logs and a quick timeline to the incident JIRA (INF-2279).

Marcus
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

Subject: Post-recovery summary and next steps — BrightHealth incident (INF-2279)

Hi Samantha —

Short summary: the rolling recovery completed successfully. Timeline highlights below and the full postmortem draft is attached.

Incident window: 2026-11-19 08:28 — 2026-11-19 10:05 PST.
Impact: up to 28% throughput degradation at peak, elevated queuing for ~55 minutes. No increase in 5xx error rates; internal retries masked some latency but customers saw slower responses.
Primary cause: KV-cache eviction storm triggered by atypical prompt-length distribution; this amplified per-worker queue depth and the autoscaler reaction window missed the transient spike.
What we did: 10% canary reroute to hosted pool, staggered rolling restarts of workers (clearing KV caches), and a temporary adjustment to the autoscaler reaction window.
Remediation (next 48–72h):
- Deploy autoscaler update to incorporate queue-length and kv-miss-rate as inputs (INF-2284).
- Add a prefix-cache warmup for identified request classes to prevent cache stampede.
- Permanently increase min-replicas for critical shard groups by 1.

Credits & billing: Monica will follow up with a proposed credit for the impacted window.

Links and artifacts:
- Postmortem draft: postmortem-draft.md (attached)
- Incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2279
- HubSpot: hubspot:deal_90123

Next steps: Monica will send a formal credit proposal and timeline for fixes; Marcus will own the autoscaler rollout; I'll run a joint RCA call on Monday (Nov 22) to walk through the timeline and mitigation plan.

Appreciate your patience and the quick approval for the canary reroute. Please reply if you'd like additional detail or a separate technical call.

Best,
